clue.text: Scrape a new beard

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of a beard are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A shaving instruction: take a razor to a freshly grown beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away a surface by rubbing, a synonym for scrape.

clue.text: Put on finery and rode out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are scattered and put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up in their best clothes and goes out riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate, so being adorned means having fine clothes or ornaments put on.

clue.text: Dance that's odd to half the band

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: half takes the first half of the letters of band

explanation.surface: A dance that seems strange to half of the musicians playing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Title of the French game

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: The name of a French sport or contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess holds a noble rank, which is a title of nobility.

clue.text: Unaltered, it's as I designed

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters were worked into a planned new order

explanation.surface: A designer insists that something has been left exactly as they drew it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left as it is remains in its original state, untouched and unchanged.

clue.text: Kipling character to watch out, in short

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the word for watch sits around the character

parts.note: to watch secretly is to spy
Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel Kim

explanation.surface: A Kipling hero is told, briefly, to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch out' reads as a warning, but 'out' puts SPY outside KIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or scanty, as in a skimpy garment that is too short.

clue.text: New master and merchant

indicators.note: new signals the letters of master and are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new master craftsman who is also a merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a shopkeeper or dealer in goods, a synonym for merchant.

clue.text: Kind of gamble is without point

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so is goes around the point

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A sort of gamble that is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort of thing, as in a species of fraud.

clue.text: Put the cards away and get ready for action

definitions.meaning: literally, sweep the playing cards off the table
the naval phrase for removing obstructions before a battle

explanation.surface: A card game ends and players prepare for something more lively.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from sailors removing clutter from a ship before fighting; literally it fits tidying cards too.

clue.text: Downfall makes temper return

indicators.note: return asks for the word to come back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: a temper or bad mood: temper means mood

explanation.surface: Someone's ruin is caused by their bad temper flaring up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is ruin or a fatal end, the same as a downfall.

clue.text: Farmed in a civilised way

definitions.meaning: land that has been tilled and grown with crops
refined, well-mannered and educated in taste

explanation.surface: Someone worked the land with refinement and good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' and 'way' only link the two senses: one agricultural, one about refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that is farmed is tilled; a refined, civilised person is likewise described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Peruvians head east as a precaution

parts.note: the Incas were the people of the ancient Peruvian empire

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Peruvian travellers set off eastwards, just to be on the safe side.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something just in case means doing it as a safeguard against a possible problem.

clue.text: For dessert, such an order can't be bettered

definitions.meaning: a sweet baked pudding of fruit in pastry

definitions.text: such an order can't be bettered
definitions.meaning: the idiom for perfect neatness, in ___ order

explanation.surface: A diner orders a pudding that cannot be improved on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-pie order' is an idiom meaning perfectly neat and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a classic fruit pudding, and also the phrase completing the idiom for perfect tidiness.

clue.text: Setback — very sad to get upset about it

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the next word
upset means the letters of very sad are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a setback and is told it is natural to be very sad about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get upset' turns VERY SAD into ADVERSY, and 'about' puts it around IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity is misfortune or hardship, and a setback is one instance of such trouble.

clue.text: Simple departure is without formality

parts.note: going is a leaving or departure

explanation.surface: An informal exit is an easy matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing person is relaxed and casual, behaving without formality.

clue.text: Military policeman is about to see mischief-makers

indicators.note: about tells us the word is goes around the letters for the policeman

parts.note: MP is the standard abbreviation for military police or policeman

explanation.surface: A military policeman is on the way to deal with some troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are small mischievous sprites, so naughty children or pranksters.

clue.text: Soft piece of cake

definitions.meaning: an undemanding, cushy option, as in a soft job

explanation.surface: A slice of sponge that is nicely soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft option and a piece of cake are both things demanding little effort.

clue.text: French aristos unable to adapt to new regimes?

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of regimes are set in a different order

explanation.surface: French nobles who could not adjust to the new revolutionary regimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to adapt to' joins definition to wordplay and paints the nobles who fled the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrés were the aristocrats who fled France during the Revolution, living in exile abroad.

clue.text: Quixotic writer never acts in play

indicators.note: in play means the letters are set moving and reshuffled

explanation.surface: An idealistic playwright never actually acts in his own play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quixotic' looks like an adjective about character, but it points to the author of Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, so he is literally the Quixote writer.

clue.text: Might it be served at a stag party?

definitions.text: Might it be served at a stag party?

parts.words: Might it be served at a stag party?
parts.note: a stag do is a groom's night out, but a stag is also a deer, whose meat might be served

explanation.surface: Wondering what food to serve at a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a groom's pre-wedding night out; read literally it is a gathering of male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of deer is the dish named, so it is literally stag served up.

clue.text: Always set out for the highest peak

indicators.note: out signals the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber always sets out for the top of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the tallest mountain on Earth.

clue.text: Strike that didn't come off?

parts.note: an industrial walkout that never happened, or a blow that missed its target

explanation.surface: A trade union's planned strike falls through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a blow with a bat or club.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly struck shot in cricket or golf is a blow that went wrong.

clue.text: I guess I'd need dressing up for masquerade

indicators.note: dressing up suggests the letters are put into a new costume or arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they will need a costume for a masked ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a false show or pretence, the same as a disguise.

clue.text: Arrested outlaw sent back to bed

indicators.note: sent back means the word is reversed, read from right to left

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: An outlaw is captured and returned to his cell bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabbed is informal for caught or seized by police, so arrested.

clue.text: Party being organised

indicators.note: organised means the letters of being are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebration is being arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spree or bout of indulgence, informally a wild party.

clue.text: Choirs take in new version of what may follow Jerusalem

indicators.note: a new version means the letters of choirs take are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choirs sing a new arrangement of the hymn Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerusalem looks like Blake's hymn, a choir staple; but Jerusalem artichokes are a root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is called the Jerusalem artichoke, so the word follows Jerusalem in its name.

clue.text: Bill's opponents

parts.note: in parliament the votes against a bill are counted as the negatives

explanation.surface: A man called Bill faces rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill reads as a man's name, but it is a parliamentary bill; those voting against it are the noes.
explanation.definitionFit: In a division of the Commons, members voting against a proposed law are recorded as the negative lobby.

clue.text: Things seen on guns

parts.note: both the scenery a tourist views and the aiming devices fitted on rifles

explanation.surface: A description of what you notice on a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both attractions viewed by tourists and the aiming devices on a firearm's barrel.

clue.text: Firm plan

definitions.meaning: resolved and determined, as in being set on doing something

explanation.surface: A company's business strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on something is being firmly resolved; one's intent is one's aim or purpose.
